searchText: Does running an eth2 node help with decentralization even if you're not validating? Is there anywhere I can read up on the economic disincentives that would discourage/prevent big validators from forming a malicious cartel and slash smaller honest validators? (Sorry if my understanding of this is totally off base) I think the case where just running a validator would improve decentralization is access to the API, right? Instead of relying on something like Infura. Right now the top 20 unique address accounts for more than 50% of validator count. Not sure if some of these address are also owned by the same person but just spread out. what impact will a much higher ETH price have on decentralization, do you think? Will people still be comfortable running and securing a validator from home when 6 figures or more are at stake? Sure as a validator thats great because you also gain more money. With the same percentage yield. Certainly, yield-wise. I was considering the security aspect - I could imagine people would rather stake custodially rather than having to safeguard their own seed and hardware, when it's about that much Also allows you to invest more of the rewards into infrastructure. The same applies to having funds on a hardware wallet to some extent, I guess But for a validator you always have 32 ETH in a single place at the start I'd imagine higher eth price will badly affect decentralization. But with the rise of staking pools (trustless) it should become better Agreed, they can't come soon enough probably answered 1000 times: where do the penalties go to? where do the slashed eth go to? Into the void burned? Yes I thought and hoped so but here it says differently https://codefi.consensys.net/blog/rewards-and-penalties-on-ethereum-20-phase-0 Slashed eth goes to whistleblower afaik oh ok In parts I think. Inactivity leak goes to nobody penalties will burn ok A small portion (1/512th) of the balance of a slashed validator goes to the block proposer (the whistle blower gets nothing in Phase 0). The slashed amount is burned, as are all penalties. so if eth stays inflationary or not depends on how validators behave basically too many bad validators --> deflationary eth Another question: we'll see increased issuance as long as eth1 is running in parallel. True? For a while, will have two distinct sources of issuance/inflation. <@!573787335796326400> I think we can assume that validators will mostly behave well. That's the whole point of the incentives and punishments. Yes - beacon chain inflation is a fraction of PoW inflation, but while both are running in parallel there will be increased issuance overall. the reason we need the 1559 for the next two years. but I get it that beacon chain inflation is a small fraction <@375471494081282048> my gut tells me that if there were so many validators getting slashed for misbehavior such that issuance turned negative, the chain would have issues with forking / finality. Meaning I don’t think it would be likely and probably lead other issues Could be wrong tho I agree <@!420951281910284289> if the chain is too unkind to stakers, then they might think of other options. But I am very optimistic right now. The penalty parameters for mainnet have also been adjusted to be less harsh against infractions, at least while validators get their bearings and the beacon chain finds stability in the first few months
